title: What an annuity is

draft.title: What an annuity is
card: An annuity is a series of equal payments made at regular intervals. The money earns compound interest, which means interest is added to the balance and then earns interest too.
Example: Sam puts $200 into a savings account at the end of every month. The payments are equal and regular, and the balance earns compound interest. This is an annuity.
An annuity can be money you pay in, such as regular saving. The payment amount and the time between payments stay the same each time.
A single deposit that is left alone is not an annuity. A set of deposits of different sizes, or made at random times, is not an annuity either.
draft.remember: An annuity is equal payments at regular intervals, earning compound interest.

a.q: Which of these is an annuity?
opts: Paying $150 into a savings account every month
Paying $5000 into a savings account once
Paying in $100, then $300, then $50 each year
Paying $150 into an account on days chosen at random
a.why: The $150 deposit every month is equal and regular, and it earns compound interest in the account. The single $5000 deposit is tempting because it earns interest, but it is only one payment, so it is not a series.
a.clue: Look for equal amounts and a regular gap.

b.q: Which of these savings plans is an annuity?
opts: Ella saves $80 at the end of each fortnight in an account
Raj deposits $1000 once and leaves it for ten years
Tia saves $50, then $70, then $90 on the first of each month
Leo deposits $60 whenever he has spare cash
b.why: Ella pays the same amount at regular intervals into an account that earns compound interest. Tia's payments are regular but they are not equal, so her plan does not fit. Raj's plan earns compound interest but has only one payment.
b.clue: Check both the size of each payment and the timing.

a.best: Paying $150 into a savings account every month

b.best: Ella saves $80 at the end of each fortnight in an account
